title: A Krull domain with Noetherian height-one prime quotients is Noetherian
statement: A commutative integral domain $D$ (a nonzero commutative ring without zero divisors), with fraction field $F=\operatorname{Frac}(D)$, is called Krull if: (i) for every height-one prime $P$ (a nonzero prime with no prime strictly between $(0)$ and $P$), $D_P$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime] is a Noetherian [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] normal domain [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring]; (ii) $D=\bigcap_{\mathrm{ht}(P)=1}D_P$ inside $F$; and (iii) every nonzero element of $D$ lies in only finitely many height-one primes. An empty intersection inside $F$ means $F$ itself. Let $D$ be a Krull domain. If $D/P$ is a Noetherian ring for every height-one prime ideal $P\subset D$, then $D$ is a Noetherian ring. No prior Noetherianity assumption on $D$, and no finite-dimensionality assumption, is imposed.

source.place: Marot, Sur les anneaux universellement japonais (1975), printed p.104, footnote (1) to Lemma 1.2: Nishimura’s general Krull-domain criterion.

proof.text: Fix a height-one prime $P$ and set $S_n=P^{(n)}=D\cap(PD_P)^n$ for $n\ge0$. The maximal-ideal contraction statement [lem-trf-localization-maximal-contraction] gives $S_1=P$, while $S_0=D$. By [lem-per-krull-symbolic-graded-embedding], each $S_n/S_{n+1}$ embeds $D$-linearly into $D/P$. A module is called Noetherian here when all its submodules are finitely generated. The $D$-submodules of $D/P$ are exactly its ideals, since the scalar action factors through the surjection $D\to D/P$. Thus the hypothesis makes $D/P$ Noetherian as a $D$-module; the injection shows that all $S_n/S_{n+1}$ are Noetherian $D$-modules as well: identify any submodule with its image ideal in $D/P$ and lift its finite generators.

source.place: Theorem 4.10.7, first two proof paragraphs, printed pp.92–93; module interpretation expanded.

proof.text: Induct on $n\ge1$ to show that $D/S_n$ is Noetherian as a $D$-module. The base case is $D/S_1=D/P$. For the step, let $N$ be any submodule of $D/S_{n+1}$ and use the natural surjection $D/S_{n+1}\to D/S_n$. Its kernel is $S_n/S_{n+1}$: a class represented by $a$ maps to zero exactly when $a\in S_n$. The intersection of $N$ with this kernel has finitely many generators by the preceding step, and the image of $N$ has finitely many generators by induction. Choose lifts in $N$ of the latter generators. These lifts together with the kernel generators generate $N$, since subtracting a combination with the same image leaves an element of the kernel. This proves the inductive assertion, without assuming $D$ Noetherian.

source.place: Theorem 4.10.7, short exact sequences and induction, printed p.93; finite-generator proof written out.

proof.text: Let $0\ne b\in D$. Apply [lem-trf-krull-principal-primary-decomposition] to obtain the finite list $P_1,\ldots,P_t$ of height-one primes containing $b$, and $bD=\bigcap_iJ_i$, with $J_i=D\cap bD_{P_i}$. Its Krull hypotheses are exactly the three conditions in our statement. If $t=0$, the empty intersection is $D$, so $bD=D$ and $D/bD=0$.

source.place: Definition 4.10.1 and Proposition 4.10.3; Theorem 4.10.7, last proof paragraph, printed p.93.

proof.text: For each listed $P_i$, [lem-weil-pbc-localization-dimension-chains-below-prime] gives $\dim D_{P_i}=1$. It is a Noetherian normal local domain by the Krull hypothesis, so [lem-sc-normal-dim1-dvr] makes it a discrete valuation ring. Choose a nonzero generator $\pi_i$ of its maximal ideal $P_iD_{P_i}$. By [lem-weil-pbc-dvr-unit-times-uniformizer-power], $b/1=u_i\pi_i^{e_i}$ with $u_i$ a unit. The element $b/1$ is nonzero because $D$ is a domain and localization is injective: if $b/1=0$, some nonzero denominator kills $b$. It lies in the maximal ideal because $b\in P_i$, so $e_i\ge1$. Consequently $bD_{P_i}=(P_iD_{P_i})^{e_i}$ and $J_i=P_i^{(e_i)}$. Step 2 therefore makes $D/J_i$ Noetherian as a $D$-module.

source.place: Theorem 4.10.7, last proof paragraph, printed p.93; Stacks Tag 00PD (lemma-characterize-dvr), conditions (5) and (4) and final assertion.

proof.text: Write $I_k=J_1\cap\cdots\cap J_k$ for $0\le k\le t$, with $I_0=D$. Induct on $k$ to show that $D/I_k$ is Noetherian as a $D$-module; for $k=0$ it is the zero module. For the step, the natural surjection $D/I_k\to D/I_{k-1}$ has kernel $I_{k-1}/I_k$. The map $I_{k-1}/I_k\to D/J_k$, $a+I_k\mapsto a+J_k$, is well defined and $D$-linear because $I_k\subseteq J_k$, and it is injective: $a\in I_{k-1}$ and $a\in J_k$ give $a\in I_k$. Since $D/J_k$ is Noetherian by Step 4, every submodule of $I_{k-1}/I_k$ is finitely generated: identify it with its image and lift finite generators. The generator-lifting argument of Step 2, with $D/I_k\to D/I_{k-1}$ in place of $D/S_{n+1}\to D/S_n$, then shows that every submodule of $D/I_k$ is finitely generated. For $k=t$, Step 3 gives $I_t=\bigcap_iJ_i=bD$. Thus $D/bD$ is Noetherian as a $D$-module for every nonzero $b$, including the unit case $t=0$, where it is $D/D=0$.

source.place: Theorem 4.10.7, last proof paragraph, printed p.93; the finite intersection of the $J_i$ handled by the same extension argument, written out.

proof.text: Finally let $I$ be any ideal of $D$. If $I=0$, the empty set generates it. Otherwise choose $0\ne b\in I$. The image $I/bD$ is a $D$-submodule of the Noetherian module $D/bD$, so has finite generators $a_1+bD,\ldots,a_r+bD$ with $a_j\in I$. For $a\in I$, subtract a $D$-linear combination of the $a_j$ with the same image in $I/bD$; the remainder belongs to $bD$. Hence $I=(b,a_1,\ldots,a_r)$. Every ideal is finitely generated, which is precisely that $D$ is Noetherian. This also handles a field: the only nonzero ideals contain a unit.

source.place: Theorem 4.10.7, final sentence, printed p.93; missing ideal-generation implication expanded.
